title_en: Guiding Case No. 214: Shanghai XX Port Industrial Co., Ltd. — case of conversion from bankruptcy liquidation to bankruptcy reorganization
ruling_gist_en:
1. When hearing bankruptcy reorganization cases involving enterprises operating river basin port terminals, the people's court shall take environmental pollution treatment as an important factor in realizing the reorganization value, and promptly eliminate the environmental pollution status that affects the continuation of the terminal operation license qualification.

2. Where an enterprise operating a port terminal causes environmental pollution due to lack of construction and maintenance of relevant infrastructure, and failure to treat it in time will affect its bankruptcy reorganization value, the administrator shall carry out treatment in accordance with the law. If the administrator requests that the relevant environmental treatment costs be treated as common benefit debts to be paid at any time from the debtor's property, the people's court shall support such request in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 214

In re Shanghai MouMou Port Industrial Co., Ltd. — Conversion from Bankruptcy Liquidation to Bankruptcy Reorganization

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on October 20, 2023)

Keywords
Civil / Application for bankruptcy liquidation / Application for bankruptcy reorganization / Pollution remediation / Common benefit debts

Ruling Gist

1. When hearing bankruptcy reorganization cases involving enterprises operating ports and wharves along river basins, the people's court shall regard pollution remediation as an important factor in realizing the reorganization value and shall promptly eliminate the pollution conditions affecting the continuation of the port operation license.

2. Where a port or wharf operating enterprise fails to construct or maintain relevant infrastructure, causing pollution, and failure to remedy in a timely manner would affect its bankruptcy reorganization value, the administrator shall carry out the remediation in accordance with the law. If the administrator requests that the related pollution remediation costs be treated as common benefit debts to be paid at any time from the debtor's property, the people's court shall support such request in accordance with the law.

Basic Facts

Shanghai MouMou Port Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai MouMou Port Co.) was established in September 1993, with its principal business being wharf leasing, warehousing, and loading/unloading services. Its location is adjacent to the mouth of the Yangtze River, bordered by the Shanghai Waigaoqiao Port Area and Free Trade Zone on the east and the Huangpu River on the west. In November 2019, upon application by a creditor, the Third Intermediate People's Court of Shanghai ruled to accept the bankruptcy liquidation case of Shanghai MouMou Port Co. Through investigation, the administrator discovered that the wharf lessee had chaotic management and outdated facilities and equipment, posing a significant hidden risk of environmental pollution. During the proceedings, the environmental protection and traffic management authorities jointly issued a rectification notice, requiring the wharf's wastewater and dust treatment facilities to be rectified within a specified time limit; otherwise, Shanghai MouMou Port Co.'s operating license would be revoked.

Shanghai MouMou Port Co. held intangible assets such as a shoreline use permit and a port operation license, and possessed 150 meters of shoreline, with water depth at the wharf front control line of 2 ≤ depth < 5 meters, and an annual cargo throughput of approximately 2 million tons. To preserve the operating value of Shanghai MouMou Port Co. and protect the interests of all creditors, the court, upon application, ruled to convert the case into reorganization proceedings.

Under the court's guidance, the administrator, on the one hand, urgently communicated and coordinated with the environmental protection and traffic management authorities to understand the specific environmental remediation requirements; on the other hand, promptly entrusted a third party to carry out construction and rectification works, including expanding and renovating facilities such as wastewater grit chambers, ditches, and ground surfaces, ensuring that rainwater, spray water, etc., from the ground were uniformly collected into the wastewater grit chamber, and after sedimentation treatment, were recycled for spraying within the port, greatly improving the port's wastewater reuse rate and effectively preventing direct discharge of wastewater into the river. Additionally, walls were installed, covers for sand and stone materials were added, and sprinkler devices for loading vehicles were installed to effectively control wharf dust and prevent excessive atmospheric pollutants in surrounding areas. When it was difficult to pay the relevant construction and cost assessment fees out of the property taken over, the administrator arranged for a third party to advance RMB 587,068, which would be repaid as common benefit debts after the reorganization funds were in place, in accordance with Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (III); part of the costs were coordinated with the lessee to be paid through rent offsets while carrying out immediate remediation.

Meanwhile, pursuant to Article 15, paragraph 1, of the same judicial interpretation, the environmental issues involved in wharf operation were fully disclosed in the creditors' meeting through a special proposal, explaining the remediation costs and their treatment, and were approved by the creditors' meeting. This effectively resolved the issue of insufficient funds for environmental remediation, improved the efficiency of pollution control, and ensured the green and environmentally friendly operation of the wharf. In the process of recruiting investors, in addition to focusing on the investors' own financial strength and corporate background, attention was also paid to their willingness and ability to operate the wharf in a green manner. Through two rounds of market-based public recruitment, investors were brought in with total investment of over RMB 87 million, and emphasis was placed on incorporating the subsequent environmental protection operation plan for the wharf into the draft reorganization plan. After reorganization, the enterprise would enhance its wharf operating capacity in three dimensions: upgrading facilities and equipment, standardized and intelligent management of the wharf, and green environmental protection operations, thereby providing supporting services for the Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone and Port Area. At the creditors' meeting, the shareholders' group failed to vote within the time limit even after exhaustive service of documents and public announcement; the secured creditors' group, tax creditors' group, and ordinary creditors' group all voted to approve the draft reorganization plan. The administrator requested the court to rule to approve the draft reorganization plan of Shanghai MouMou Port Co.

Judgment

The Third Intermediate People's Court of Shanghai, on August 10, 2022, issued civil ruling (2019) Hu 03 Po 320-6: 1. Approving the revised "Reorganization Plan (Draft) of Shanghai MouMou Port Industrial Co., Ltd."; 2. Terminating the reorganization proceedings of Shanghai MouMou Port Co. During the execution of the reorganization plan, with the assistance of the court and the administrator, the enterprise successfully resolved the issues of the expiration of its business license and the extension of its port operation license.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that when examining and approving a draft reorganization plan, the court must respect the autonomy of the creditors' meeting, adhere to the principle of legality review, and also consider whether it can achieve the maximization of social value on the basis of balancing interests. In this case, the recovery ratio for the ordinary creditors group increased from zero under the simulated liquidation; given that Shanghai MouMou Port Co. was severely insolvent, the plan adjusting the equity interest of the shareholders' group to zero was fair and reasonable. The business plan in the draft was feasible, could effectively continue the operating value of Shanghai MouMou Port Co., and help restore its operating capacity. The application of the bankruptcy administrator complied with legal provisions and was conducive to achieving the dual effect of sustainable development and ecological environment protection, and thus should be granted. The people's court should fully utilize the function of bankruptcy adjudication, integrate the concept of green development throughout the entire judicial process of reorganization, and explore the establishment of a flexible and efficient working mechanism in aspects such as the remediation of environmental issues, fee arrangements, formulation and execution of reorganization plans, making reorganization an effective path to promote the green and low-carbon transformation of distressed enterprises. The specific points are as follows:

(1) Regarding the responsibility for environmental pollution remediation and the nature of costs of an enterprise undergoing reorganization. Pursuant to relevant legal provisions such as the Environmental Protection Law of the PRC and the Port Law of the PRC, and the principle of "who pollutes, who remediates," an enterprise's responsibility for pollution remediation continues after its bankruptcy case is accepted. If a port or wharf enterprise undergoing reorganization causes environmental pollution due to lack of construction or maintenance of relevant infrastructure, it shall be the subject responsible for remediation. The administrator, as the executor of bankruptcy affairs, shall be responsible for carrying out the specific remediation actions. Such actions preserve the debtor enterprise's operating qualifications, sustain its operating value, and enhance the recovery interests of all creditors. The costs incurred for such remediation are for the benefit of all creditors. If the administrator requests that such costs be recognized as common benefit debts pursuant to Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (III), the people's court shall support such request.

(2) Regarding the path of pollution remediation during reorganization. The pollution at the wharf involved in this case mainly manifested in water and air pollution. Under the guidance of the court, the administrator coordinated to advance pollution remediation and reorganization proceedings in accordance with the law: First, government-court coordination. The court and the administrator visited local sub-districts, towns, and environmental supervision authorities to fully understand the environmental protection responsibility requirements for the involved shoreline and the subsequent planning prospects. Through communication and coordination, the relevant authorities extended the rectification period, buying time for pollution remediation. Second, immediate remediation. When the rectification notice was issued, the administrator had not taken over any rent receivables or other funds. To complete various pollution remediation measures within a short time and preserve the enterprise's operating qualifications, the administrator communicated with the wharf lessee to first entrust a third-party professional organization to carry out rectification according to standards. Through the expansion and improvement of the wastewater grit chamber and ancillary facilities, the problem of rainwater and site wastewater seeping into environmental water bodies without treatment was solved, and the wastewater reuse rate was increased. By installing dust and noise reduction equipment, air dust pollution was reduced, air quality guaranteed, and the ecological environment quality of the Yangtze River estuary basin improved. Third, cost implementation. The main costs were advanced by the lessee and later repaid as common benefit debts after the reorganization funds were in place, solving the difficulty of funding remediation. Fourth, information disclosure. Fully respecting the creditors' rights to know, participate, and supervise, and pursuant to Article 15, paragraph 1, of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (III), the pollution remediation matters were treated as material dispositions of property for a special vote. In the draft reorganization plan, the process of pollution remediation and the assumption of costs were disclosed, and the creditors' support and cooperation with the reorganization work were sought.

(3) Regarding the relationship between pollution remediation and the preservation of reorganization value. In this case, pollution remediation is closely related to the enterprise's reorganization value and is a key factor determining whether the enterprise can realize its reorganization value. Once the enterprise violates laws and regulations on pollution prevention and control and faces the penalty of being deprived of its administrative license qualifications, its reorganization value will be lost. Therefore, in the course of hearing port and wharf enterprise bankruptcy reorganization cases, attention should be paid to organically combining pollution remediation with the preservation of reorganization value, promptly eliminating pollution conditions affecting the continuation of the port operation license, and regarding pollution remediation as an important factor in realizing reorganization value.

(4) Regarding the formulation, approval, and execution of the reorganization plan. When formulating the reorganization plan, the principle of green development should be reflected, guiding investors to incorporate environmental protection operation plans and environmental commitments into the plan, and focusing on whether the enterprise can fulfill its environmental responsibilities and promote the coordinated development of economy, society, and environment in the future. When examining and approving the draft reorganization plan, legal factors such as the enterprise's liquidation value and procedural legality should be comprehensively considered, as well as social factors such as the enterprise's sustainable development and ecological environment protection. During the execution of the reorganization plan, obstacles to the enterprise's continued operation should be resolved. By exploring a new mechanism for the coordinated advancement of bankruptcy adjudication and judicial protection of the ecological environment, source control of pollution and carbon emission reduction in the Yangtze River basin and the green and low-carbon transformation of enterprises can be achieved, promoting the organic unity of ecological environment protection, enterprise rebirth, and maximization of creditors' interests.

Relevant Legal Provisions

1. Article 73 of the Yangtze River Protection Law of the People's Republic of China
2. Articles 42 and 43 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China
